newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street seen mixed to higher at open.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street seen mixed to higher at open.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were expected to open mixed to slightly higher on Thursday, with bargain-hunters stepping in after yesterday's volatile session which ultimately pushed share prices lower.

While the broader market might move higher, analysts said the technology sector could come under some pressure after several earnings warnings. A big swing in the initial jobless claims could also derail the bond and stock market, they said.
"Unless we have a wild claims number, we should see some bargain hunting and the market could open a little higher," Richard Cripps, chief market strategist at Legg Mason Wood Walker, said.
In early trade, the Standard & Poor's 500 futures index was up 1.45 points at 897.70, while the long bond was unchanged at a 6.74 percent yield.
On Wednesday, U.S. stocks slumped amid a sell-off in bonds and concerns that higher oil prices might fuel inflation.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average finished down 68.08 points at 7689.98.
